key_insight: CloudCons shows that better zero-shot forecasting does not automatically produce better cloud consolidation decisions, so evaluation must be end-to-end, not just prediction-focused.
engineering_relevance: For cloud operators, the benchmark helps choose forecasting models and predictive quantiles that jointly improve resource efficiency while maintaining service reliability.
method: Built an end-to-end benchmark for forecast-then-optimize cloud resource consolidation.
Curated diverse real-world datasets from Huawei Cloud, Microsoft Azure, and Google Borg.
Compared statistical, deep learning, and foundation models using decision-utility outcomes, not only forecast error.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that foundation models achieve superior zero-shot forecasting accuracy, but this advantage does not necessarily translate into better consolidation utility across workloads with diurnal rhythms, bursty pulses, and high-frequency noise.
watch_item: Forecast accuracy can be misleading for deployment: predictive quantile choice strongly affects the efficiency-reliability trade-off and must be calibrated for the target workload.
paper_title: CloudCons: A Comprehensive End-to-End Benchmark for Cloud Resource Consolidation
